labels: All numbers are proposed design targets. They are living people; the dead of Volgan and Zol are not counted.

world.note: A pre-modern world after seventeen centuries of peace, better farming (Second Age) and medicine; a little above medieval Europe at its peak.

Middle Lands.density_note: Great Lake basin and plains: the best fed land of Aoaz; about 40 to 55 people per square kilometre on the plains and up to 110 beside the Aenar, the Great River and the Great Lake shore.
Middle Lands.character: The most fertile and populous land by density; Aenor and the Concord dominions; many cities around the lake.

East Lands.density_note: Rivers and oases carry the people; the deserts hold almost none. River valleys and lake shores run 70 to 110 per square kilometre; the open desert under one.
East Lands.character: The richest and most divided land: river kingdoms, caravan cities, desert tribes.

Cold Lands.density_note: The largest landmass but sparse: coastal and valley farms 12 to 20 per square kilometre, the interior under two, the far north-west almost none.
Cold Lands.character: Sparse but hardy; clans, herds, western ports; the far north holds the silent castle.

West Lands.density_note: Temperate hills and river plains: 20 to 35 per square kilometre.
West Lands.character: Clan hills, river towns, guild ports.

North Lands.density_note: Coastal belts and fjord valleys: 15 to 30 per square kilometre.
North Lands.character: Sea-crowns on the strait and small hill kingdoms.

Lands of the Sun.density_note: Very fertile but thinly peopled: the Sunhot elves are few and long-lived; 10 to 20 per square kilometre.
Lands of the Sun.character: Sun-blessed fields; elves in sanctuaries; Gala; the three realms of Sunfolk.

Dark Lands.density_note: Hills, forest, marsh and volcano: 6 to 14 per square kilometre.
Dark Lands.character: Orc holds, Dondor, the troll forest, volcano country.

Magical Lands.density_note: Rich forest land held by long-lived elves: 4 to 8 per square kilometre in the realms, near nothing in the black areas.
Magical Lands.character: Elven realms in groves; the Wall; Dragon Mountain; the Worshipdom valleys.

Triton's Islands.density_note: Small islands, fully used coasts: 25 to 40 per square kilometre on inhabited isles.
Triton's Islands.character: Chart-houses and corsair isles; harbour towns.

Ember Lands.density_note: Hot desert and hills, storm-girt coasts: lake country and the north coast 8 to 15, the interior under one.
Ember Lands.character: Thin: Mirolon's lake country, coast freeholds, the Nether realms and Volgan's hosts (the dead are not counted).

Islands of the South.density_note: Reef islands with fishing coasts: 20 to 35 per square kilometre.

Zol's Mistake.density_note: Black wasteland: 0.02 per square kilometre outside Furviatlon.
Zol's Mistake.character: Nearly empty; only the town of Furviatlon and a few fishers on the islands; the dead are not counted.

density_modifiers.note: The river and lake rule follows the geography model (05_geography_model.md section 5: population doubled within 40 pixels of a river of width 2 or more or a lake). Elves and other long-lived peoples multiply the density of their land by the people factor because they are few. A state with a mixed population uses the weighted mean.

state_population_rule: state_people = region_calibration × Σ over land provinces of (province_area × density_class(terrain) × river/lake/coast/crossroads modifiers × fertility × history × people_factor). region_calibration is chosen so that the region total equals the region target within 1%. Settlements of the settlement list are then added on top as their stated sizes minus the people already counted for their province.

categories.rule: state_people under 25,000 and no settlement of 5,000
island of two to four provinces
island of five or more provinces
largest settlement 5,000 to 20,000, or 150,000 to 280,000 people
largest settlement 100,000 to 250,000, or a regional capital
largest settlement 250,000 or more, or a great power capital with 100,000 or more

game_numbers.manpower_per_state: state manpower = state_people × 0.11 (the share of men of fighting age who could be raised in a war); a people may multiply it by its recruitable_population_factor.
game_numbers.resource_rule: Resources keep the economy spec's region weights; population does not change them. Essence and Gold stay scarce.
game_numbers.starting_factories: workshops = urban_people ÷ 75,000 × (region_dev ÷ 0.60); armouries = workshops × 0.45 in Aenor and Lerendor, × 0.55 in orc and Volgan lands, × 0.5 elsewhere; shipwrights = coastal urban_people ÷ 400,000. Round to the nearest whole building; no factory in a state under 25,000 people.
game_numbers.infrastructure: infrastructure level = 1 + floor(density rank of the state in its region ÷ 0.25); roads follow settlement size (a settlement of 20,000 or more has level 3; of 100,000 or more level 4); the Restoration roads give the Middle Lands +1.

starting_class_targets.class: Great power of men (Lerendor, Coldor, Noris, Stabilo, Gunwaith)
Orc and dark great powers (Goldoroth, Volgan)

game_numbers.principle: A country's strength follows its land, its rivers and its trade. The class table gives the usual outcome of the formulas. It is never a target to be forced.

minorities_and_borders.rows: Aenor holds many dominions of its own culture; the Selen, Kilinti and Hiloron border has men, ents and giants living side by side; the south marches mix march-folk with refugees from the Ember Lands coast; the Veiled and Redbark are enclaves inside Aenor's roads.
The strait coast is Leren; the inland crowns are Free Crowns; Blackton on the Dark Lands coast is mixed Dondor and Leren; Leren sailors settle R'en.
Gunwaith clans and Girdon wardens mix along the Grey Ford; guild towns have Aenoran merchants; Buldor companies recruit from every clan.
Ice clans mix with yeti and giants at the high valleys; Windwaith and the western ports have Gunwaithic traders.
Goblins live in orc holds, trolls in the Troll Forest; Dondor and Blackton hold human towns beside orc hills; Belonton and the sea orcs share islands with Leren fishers.
Mushroom-forest mycids live inside an elven realm [O]; the Worshipdom valleys are men inside the elven region; the rift coast has Alerhic merchants.
Noric, Stabilic and Alerhic peoples mix at the crossroads; caravan towns host every tongue; the Hidden Council's eastern clients are present in every city. [secret]
The Sunfolk of Goodin live among the Sunhot; the Gala court has a few men and Sunhot courtiers.
Mirolon's wardens, coast freeholders and the Nether realms; Volgan's Dominion holds orcs, ogres and demons beside the dead.

core_and_claim_logic: Every country cores its own states at the start. No claims at the start (foundation spec).

A people that lived in a state before a conquest keeps it as a cultural claim for play: the Gunwaith claim nothing from Aenor at the start but resent its old charts; the Veiled and Redbark never accept Aenor's authority; Leren crowns resist Lerendor's supremacy but accept its protection.

Resistance follows culture: a state of a different culture than its ruler's adds +20% resistance target; a state of a people of Great Folk ruled by Common Folk adds +10%; a state whose faith differs from the ruler's adds +5%; the Wall-Folk and Lake Aenorans treat each other as one culture.
